author: Matt Wolfe
description:
I vibe coded a free productivity app that keeps my entire business in one place, and I built it so anyone can download and customize it. I already use an earlier version of this dashboard every day, but this time I rebuilt it from scratch to see how far I could push Codex on a genuinely useful business tool. I used Codex inside ChatGPT for the initial build, then spent hours testing, debugging, and refining it.

The result is Control Center: one dashboard for industry news, brand mentions, reminders, audience analytics, newsletters, and recurring tasks. It connects to Gmail, tracks social growth across YouTube, X, Instagram, and more, and can optionally use OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, Grok, or local models to rank and summarize what matters. No AI API key is required. You can install it locally from GitHub for free, customize every section, and optionally host it online.

Download your own control center on GitHub: http://github.com/mreflow/control-center

title: I Built a FREE App That Runs Your Entire Business

author: Matt Wolfe
description:
You don’t need a massive GPU server to run powerful AI models locally anymore.

Models like Qwen 3.8 27B can run on consumer-grade computers, and LM Studio makes the whole process ridiculously easy.

You just search for the model → choose the highest-quality quantization your computer can handle → download it → start chatting.

LM Studio will even tell you whether a specific version should run on your machine before you download it.

Local models keep getting smaller, more efficient, and more capable. Combined with the extra layer of privacy and data security, it's natural that people are becoming more and more interested in them. 

Are you making the switch to local AI, or are cloud models like ChatGPT and Claude still the best?
